### MongoDB query operators, index bounds and projection

- **MongoDB query operators, index bounds and projection** · self

### query operator anti-pattern

- **query operator anti-pattern** · problem · aka: anti-pattern, anti-patterns, antipattern, unanchored regex, $regex, regular expression, case-insensitive regex, prefix expression, $ne, $nin, $not, negation, negated, inequality operator, $exists, $where, $expr, sargable, non-sargable

### $in

- **$in** · part — The $in behavior change at 201 array elements is not guaranteed to stay the same for all MongoDB versions. · aka: $in operator, $or operator, $or clauses, clauses of $or, SUBPLAN, subplanner, index union, union of index scans, $or query, $or queries, $in list, $in array — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/

### projection

- **projection** · part — The document with `_id` equal to `3` is the only document that matched the [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemmatch.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-elemMatch) criteria. · aka: project fields, projected fields, return only, exclude _id, _id: 0, $slice, $elemMatch projection, projection pushdown, covered query, covered queries, PROJECTION_COVERED, PROJECTION_SIMPLE, PROJECTION_DEFAULT — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch.md#elemmatch-https-www-mongodb-com-docs-manual-reference-operator-projection-elemmatch-md-mongodb-projection-proj-elemmatch-with-multiple-fields

### count

- **count** · part · aka: countDocuments, estimatedDocumentCount, count(), db.collection.count, $count, COUNT_SCAN, count operations, db.collection.distinct, distinct(), DISTINCT_SCAN, $sample, random sample, pseudo-random cursor

### cursor

- **cursor** · part — The pseudo-random cursor walks the B-tree and is not guaranteed uniform; skew is likelier with unbalanced trees, many deleted documents, or many documents invisible to the transaction. For a uniform sample put another stage (such as $match) before $sample or use N above 5%, accepting the scan. · aka: batchSize, batch size, cursor.batchSize, getMore, firstBatch, maxTimeMS, cursor.maxTimeMS, noCursorTimeout, cursor timeout, cursorTimeoutMillis, tailable cursor, maxAwaitTimeMS, exhaust cursor — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample/

### read preference

- **read preference** · related · aka: readPreference, read preferences, secondary reads, secondaryPreferred, nearest, read concern, readConcern, local read concern, majority read concern, causal consistency

### sharded query targeting

- **sharded query targeting** · part · aka: targeted query, targeted queries, targeted operations, scatter-gather, scatter gather, broadcast operations, broadcast query, query router, mongos, SHARD_MERGE, SHARDING_FILTER, shard targeting, single shard, all shards, merge on mongos, $lookup on sharded, include the shard key, shard key in the query, query isolation

### query shape

- **query shape** · related — A query shape is a set of specifications that group similar queries together. Specifications can include filters, sorts, projections, aggregation pipeline stages, a namespace, and others. Queries that have similar specifications have the same query shape. · aka: query shapes, query pattern, query patterns, query predicate, query selector — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/

### index

- **index** · related — - Indexes are not used for comparisons where the `let` operand resolves to an empty or missing value. · aka: indexes, indexed, IXSCAN, COLLSCAN, collection scan, explain, executionStats, winningPlan — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#expr-in-lookup-operations

### query optimization

- **query optimization** · hypernym — Query optimization improves the efficiency of read operations by reducing the amount of data that query operations need to process. Use indexes, projections, and query limits to enhance query performance and reduce resource consumption. · aka: query performance, optimize queries, query optimizer, analyze query performance — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/
